cause: Both gen_unix_timestamps clamped start to 1970 and read epoch through timestamp() on naive values, so ranges before 1970 raised or were dropped
context: Operator confirmed 2026-10-24, answer verbatim: "Confirmo, HIGH, já (Recomendado)"; by-name approval of NPCore.gen_unix_timestamps and SparkCore.gen_unix_timestamps (invariant 12): "Aprovo os dois (Recomendado)". Breaks constitution invariant 3 (a spec that validates generates). NumPy and Spark share the clamp (rand_engine/core/_spark_core.py SparkCore.gen_unix_timestamps). Reproduced on feature/0.8.1 c1660e6 and on the released 0.8.0 wheel.
expected: Every range that validates generates values inside [start, end), including dates from 1900 (negative epoch seconds), on NumPy and Spark; ranges entirely after 1970 keep their seeded values.
repro: PYTHONPATH=repos/rand-engine uv run --no-project --with numpy==2.1.3 --with pandas==2.2.3 --with pyarrow==23.0.1 python -c "from rand_engine import DataGenerator; DataGenerator({'d':{'method':'dates','kwargs':{'start':'1950-01-01','end':'1960-12-31'}}},seed=1).size(10).get_df()" (exit 1, ValueError: high <= 0)
solution: Epoch seconds by UTC timedelta arithmetic, clamp deleted, in NPCore and SparkCore
symptom: A spec with start 1950-01-01 and end 1960-12-31 validates, then get_df raises ColumnGenerationError: ValueError: high <= 0. A range 1960-01-01..1980-12-31 validates and returns min 1970-01-01: dates before 1970 are dropped without notice.
title: dates and unix_timestamps before 1970 validate, then raise or silently clamp to 1970
